definition: Attention mechanisms that limit each token's attention computation to a subset of other tokens, rather than the full sequence, to reduce computational cost.
details: Sparse attention patterns (such as local windows or strided patterns) allow transformers to scale to much longer context lengths than standard full (quadratic-cost) self-attention would allow.

explainer.lead: Sparse attention restricts each token's attention computation to a subset of other tokens instead of the full sequence. It matters because it lets transformers scale to far longer contexts than full self-attention permits.

tiers.eli5: Instead of every word in a long document talking to every other word, each word only chats with a nearby handful—so the conversation stays manageable.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick a sparsity pattern such as local windows or strided patterns to cut cost at long context lengths. The pitfall is choosing a pattern that never connects tokens that need to interact.
tiers.paperLevel: Attention where each token attends to only a subset of tokens rather than the full sequence; the standard full self-attention it replaces has quadratic cost.

explainer.example: With a local-window pattern, each token attends only to the tokens within a fixed distance, so cost grows linearly rather than quadratically with sequence length.
